title: Common-resolution formulas for two triple direct-image paths
statement:
Let $X_0\xrightarrow fX_1\xrightarrow gX_2\xrightarrow hX_3$ be morphisms of ringed topoi presented by small sites with sheaves of commutative rings [def-weil-pbc-ringed-topos-morphism]. Use their module sheaf categories [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], ordinary unbounded derived categories, and localizations $Q_i:K(\operatorname{Mod}(X_i))\to D(\operatorname{Mod}(X_i))$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Put $R_f=Rf_*$, and analogously for composites. Use the normalized natural comparisons $\kappa_{b,a}:R_{ba}\xrightarrow{\sim}R_bR_a$ of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-pushforward-composition], and the canonical resolution identifications of [lem-sf-kinjective-derived-map-computation]. All underived composition identifications are the canonical ones, and functor associators are suppressed.
Let $I$ be K-injective on $X_0$ and choose K-injective resolutions $j:f_*I\to J$ on $X_1$, $k:g_*J\to K$ and $t:g_*f_*I\to T$ on $X_2$ [def-pur-kinjective-complex]. Then $g_*j$ and $k\circ g_*j$ are quasi-isomorphisms. There is a unique homotopy class of chain maps $u:T\to K$ such that
$$Q_2u=Q_2(k\circ g_*j)\circ(Q_2t)^{-1},\qquad u\circ t\simeq k\circ g_*j.$$
Set $\alpha=(R_h\kappa_{g,f})\circ\kappa_{h,gf}$ and $\beta=(\kappa_{h,g}R_f)\circ\kappa_{hg,f}$. Identify their common source $R_{hgf}(Q_0I)$ with $Q_3(h_*g_*f_*I)$ using $I$, and their common target $R_hR_gR_f(Q_0I)$ with $Q_3(h_*K)$ using $j$ and $k$. In precisely these coordinates their components are
$$\alpha_{Q_0I}=Q_3(h_*u)\circ Q_3(h_*t),\qquad
\beta_{Q_0I}=Q_3(h_*k)\circ Q_3(h_*g_*j).$$
More explicitly, $\kappa_{h,gf}$ is represented by $h_*t$; the map $R_h(\kappa_{g,f,Q_0I})$, using $t$ and $k$ to resolve its source and target, is represented by $h_*u$; $\kappa_{hg,f}$ is represented by $h_*g_*j$; and $\kappa_{h,g}$ at $R_f(Q_0I)$, after the identification induced by $j$, is represented by $h_*k$. The formulas hold for every choice of $j,k,t$ with the canonical resolution transitions. Neither $f_*I$ nor $g_*J$ is assumed K-injective, and no module direct image is assumed to preserve K-injectives.

source.place: Tag 0D6E, lemma-derived-pushforward-composition; agent extraction of the two triple-path component formulas on a common K-injective resolution

proof.text: All four module categories have K-injective resolutions by [prop-pur-kinjective-resolutions-exist]: the sites are small and the ring sheaves are commutative, exactly as required there. The induced module direct images are additive by [def-weil-pbc-ringed-topos-morphism]. Thus the unbounded derived-map computation applies to each of them. Write $\eta_x$ for the derived unit of $x_*$ and, for K-injective $L$ on its domain, put $e_{x,L}=\eta_{x,L}^{-1}:R_x(Q L)\xrightarrow{\sim}Q(x_*L)$. The inverse exists by [def-sfb-right-derived-functor]. Put $A=f_*I$, $B=g_*A$, $C=g_*J$ and $p=g_*j:B\to C$. No assertion that $A$ or $C$ is K-injective is used. Lean implementation: apply Grothendieck abelianness from the universe-independent resolution theorem on the three source sites. The source-library HasKInjectiveResolutions instance and CategoryTheory.derives, together with LocalizerMorphism.Derives.isIso_of_isRightDerivedFunctor, evaluate each of the six supplied derived units invertibly on the needed K-injectives.

source.place: Tags 070Y (lemma-K-injective-defined) and 070K (lemma-enough-K-injectives-implies); module-sheaf existence from sites-cohomology.tex Section 07A5 and injectives.tex Tag 079P

proof.text: Apply the normalization of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-pushforward-composition] to $(f,g)$, the K-injective $I$, and its supplied resolution $j:f_*I\to J$. It says explicitly that $p=g_*j$ is a quasi-isomorphism. Since $k:C\to K$ is a quasi-isomorphism by hypothesis, $w=k\circ p:B\to K$ is one too: in every degree its cohomology map is the composite of the two invertible cohomology maps, by [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Thus $w$ and $t$ are both K-injective resolutions of $B$, although $B$ itself need not be K-injective. More directly for the supplied comparisons: naturality along j and the given unit normalization give v.inv followed by kappa_gf followed by b.hom = Qp. All three factors are isomorphisms; the localization criterion implies p is a quasi-isomorphism.

source.place: Tag 0D6E, lemma-derived-pushforward-composition, with its normalized comparison as stated in the cited DAG node

proof.text: The Hom bijection of [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-hom-derived], with source $T$ and K-injective target $K$, lifts the derived morphism $Q_2w\circ(Q_2t)^{-1}$ to a unique homotopy class $u:T\to K$. Applying the same bijection with source $B$ and target $K$, the equality $Q_2(ut)=Q_2w$ implies $ut\simeq w$. Conversely, this homotopy implies the displayed formula for $Q_2u$ after cancellation of $Q_2t$, proving the asserted uniqueness with both conditions.

source.place: Tag 070I, lemma-K-injective, clauses (2),(3) and their application to the two K-injective resolutions

proof.text: Spell out the coordinates, writing composition right to left. Set $a=(Q_1j)e_{f,I}:R_f(Q_0I)\xrightarrow{\sim}Q_1J$, $v=e_{gf,I}:R_{gf}(Q_0I)\xrightarrow{\sim}Q_2B$, and $b=e_{g,J}R_g(a):R_gR_f(Q_0I)\xrightarrow{\sim}Q_2C$. Put $s=e_{hgf,I}$, $E_t=e_{h,T}R_h(Q_2t)$ and $E_k=e_{h,K}R_h(Q_2k)$. These are precisely $c_t,c_k$ for $h_*$ in [lem-sf-kinjective-derived-map-computation]. Then $m=E_tR_h(v)$ identifies $R_hR_{gf}(Q_0I)$ with $Q_3(h_*T)$, and $d=E_kR_h(b)=e_{h,K}R_h((Q_2k)b)$ identifies the final target $R_hR_gR_f(Q_0I)$ with $Q_3(h_*K)$. Thus $s$ is the source coordinate of the question and $d$ is exactly its target coordinate obtained successively from $j,k$. All these maps are isomorphisms: the $e$ maps are evaluation on K-injectives, and $j,k,t$ are quasi-isomorphisms.

source.place: Tag 070Y, lemma-K-injective-defined; substitution in the canonical resolution formula of the cited derived-map node

proof.text: The $(f,g)$ normalization gives $b\,\kappa_{g,f,Q_0I}\,v^{-1}=Q_2p$. For the first outer comparison use the same theorem on the pair $(gf,h)$ with K-injective $I$ and the resolution $t:B\to T$. Its target coordinate is $e_{h,T}R_h((Q_2t)v)=m$, so it gives $m\,\kappa_{h,gf,Q_0I}\,s^{-1}=Q_3(h_*t)$. Here all underived compositions are identified canonically, as required in the statement; this is a direct use of the two-functor normalization, not an assumption about associativity of three derived comparisons.

source.place: Tag 0D6E, lemma-derived-pushforward-composition; normalized pair comparisons applied to (f,g) and (gf,h)

proof.text: Apply [lem-sf-kinjective-derived-map-computation] with additive functor $h_*$, derived morphism $Q_2p:Q_2B\to Q_2C$, and resolutions $t:B\to T$, $k:C\to K$. The class computing that map is exactly $u$, because its required equation is $Q_2u=(Q_2k)(Q_2p)(Q_2t)^{-1}$. Hence $E_kR_h(Q_2p)E_t^{-1}=Q_3(h_*u)$. Substituting the preceding equation for $Q_2p$ and the definitions of $d,m$ gives $d\,R_h(\kappa_{g,f,Q_0I})\,m^{-1}=Q_3(h_*u)$. Multiply this by the second equation of the preceding step and cancel $m^{-1}m$. This gives $d\,\alpha_{Q_0I}\,s^{-1}=Q_3(h_*u)\circ Q_3(h_*t)$ and identifies each of its two factors exactly as claimed. Different representatives of $u$ give the same map: applying an additive functor to the chain-homotopy equation applies $h_*$ to its homotopy in each degree. The Lean proof establishes the arbitrary-unit version directly, avoiding transport from the chosen universal pair of the dependency: choose a chain-map representative of u using fullness of the homotopy quotient, translate its Qh equation through quotientCompQhIso, and apply naturality of eta_h. The private coordinate_map lemma then cancels the resolution and coordinate isomorphisms. This gives exactly the same map computation and requires no extra hypothesis.

source.place: Tag 070Y, lemma-K-injective-defined; arbitrary-derived-morphism computation, specialized to h_* with resolutions t and k

proof.text: Set $r=e_{hg,J}R_{hg}(a):R_{hg}R_f(Q_0I)\xrightarrow{\sim}Q_3(h_*C)$. Apply the pair normalization to $(f,hg)$ with $I,j$ to get $r\,\kappa_{hg,f,Q_0I}\,s^{-1}=Q_3(h_*p)$. Next apply it to $(g,h)$ with K-injective $J$ and the resolution $k:g_*J\to K$. Writing $\kappa_{h,g,Q_1J}$ for its component, it says $E_kR_h(e_{g,J})\,\kappa_{h,g,Q_1J}\,e_{hg,J}^{-1}=Q_3(h_*k)$. Naturality of $\kappa_{h,g}$ at $a:R_f(Q_0I)\to Q_1J$ reads $R_hR_g(a)\,\kappa_{h,g,R_f(Q_0I)}=\kappa_{h,g,Q_1J}\,R_{hg}(a)$. Substitute this equality and $d=E_kR_h(e_{g,J})R_hR_g(a)$; cancellation of $R_{hg}(a)$ proves $d\,\kappa_{h,g,R_f(Q_0I)}\,r^{-1}=Q_3(h_*k)$. Multiplying the two displayed coordinate equations proves $d\,\beta_{Q_0I}\,s^{-1}=Q_3(h_*k)\circ Q_3(h_*g_*j)$. Thus the second path uses the very same source $s$ and target $d$ as the first path.

source.place: Tag 0D6E, lemma-derived-pushforward-composition; normalization at (f,hg) and (g,h), and naturality explicitly included in the cited node

proof.text: The choices in the argument were arbitrary. To check the specified transitions, let $j',k',t'$ be other choices and use primes for their coordinates. A change of $t$ has intermediate transition $m'm^{-1}=E_{t'}E_t^{-1}$, exactly the canonical transition of [lem-sf-kinjective-derived-map-computation]. It appears on the left of the first factor of the alpha path and with its inverse on the right of the second factor, so cancels in their product. For a simultaneous change of $j,k$, that node applied to the derived map $b'b^{-1}:Q_2C\to Q_2C'$ with resolutions $k,k'$ identifies $d'd^{-1}=E_{k'}R_h(b'b^{-1})E_k^{-1}$ with $Q_3(h_*z)$, where $Q_2z=(Q_2k')b'b^{-1}(Q_2k)^{-1}$ is the unique homotopy class $K\to K'$. This is the canonical final-target transition and has the cocycle and intertwining properties stated there. Indeed each full path $P$ changes its matrix by $d'Ps^{-1}=(d'd^{-1})(dPs^{-1})$. These equations cover arbitrary simultaneous choices and prove the required compatibility. Only $I,J,K,T$ were used as K-injectives; no direct-image preservation of that property was invoked. In Lean the same private coordinate_map argument applies with identity derived morphism and equal coordinates v,v for the t-transition, and coordinates b,b-prime for the simultaneous j,k-transition. Qh_map_bijective supplies existence and uniqueness of each homotopy class; cancellation proves its computed image equation.
